description: This penitential selihah survives in several manuscripts found in the Cairo Geniza. It is based on the conceit that the Jewish people is “sick”—that is, suffering in exile—and that God can heal this illness by bringing redemption. Aaron Ibn al-‘Ammānī (12th century) signed his given name twice in the acrostic of this poem. Each line in this rhythmic and compressed work has three internal rhymes, precisely sixteen syllables, and ends with the word holeh (ill). (Information from Posen Library)
